title: Factorization retracts from left and right lifting
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category], and let $A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C$ and $f:A\to C$ satisfy $pi=f$. A map $j:U\to V$ has the left lifting property against $q:X\to Y$ when every pair $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$ with $qa=bj$ admits $d:V\to X$ with $dj=a$ and $qd=b$. A morphism $f:A\to C$ is an arrow retract of $g:A'\to C'$ when there exist $a:A\to A'$, $b:C\to C'$, $r:A'\to A$, $s:C'\to C$ with $ga=bf$, $fr=sg$, $ra=1_A$ and $sb=1_C$. If $f$ has the left lifting property against $p$, there is $d:C\to B$ with $df=i$ and $pd=1_C$; $f$ is an arrow retract of $i$ by the arrow maps $(1_A,d):f\to i$ and $(1_A,p):i\to f$. If $i$ has the left lifting property against $f$, there is $e:B\to A$ with $ei=1_A$ and $fe=p$; $f$ is an arrow retract of $p$ by the arrow maps $(i,1_C):f\to p$ and $(e,1_C):p\to f$.
